stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple’s stock is up 2.6% on the day and 7.2% over the month, still 4.3% below its 52‑week high but 43.9% above its low, indicating room for upside toward the peak. The recent rally is driven by strong earnings momentum, and investors should watch the upcoming product cycle and any guidance on services revenue.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft slipped 1.2% today but remains 6.8% under its 52‑week high, holding a solid 42.3% gain from its low. Momentum is modest, and the next catalyst is the Q3 earnings beat and cloud‑services guidance, especially Azure consumption trends.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: NVIDIA fell 1.5% on the day, sitting 7.7% shy of its 52‑week high while still 31.8% above its low, reflecting a healthy mid‑range position. The key watch is the next AI‑related earnings update and inventory trends in its data‑center segment.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet is down 1.3% today and 10.3% over the month, trading 16.7% below its 52‑week high but 59% above its low, suggesting a broad discount. Investors should focus on the upcoming ad‑spend recovery data and any progress on AI product rollouts.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon slipped 1.9% today, 10.2% under its 52‑week high yet 28.2% above its low, indicating a modestly discounted valuation. The next driver will be the holiday‑season sales outlook and cloud‑growth metrics from AWS.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta rose 1.1% on the day, still 25.6% below its 52‑week high but only 10.1% above its low, reflecting a steep decline from its peak. Watch the rollout of AI features in its apps and the next earnings for signs of revenue stabilization.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla fell 3.2% today, 27.3% under its 52‑week high while 19.4% above its low, showing a sizable gap to its peak. The pivotal factor is the upcoming production updates and demand trends for the new model line‑up.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom dipped 0.2% today, 23.1% below its 52‑week high and 26.2% above its low, holding a modest upside potential. Investors should monitor the next quarterly earnings for guidance on its semiconductor and infrastructure software segments.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD dropped 2.4% on the day, 20.9% under its 52‑week high but still 204.1% above its low, reflecting a strong long‑term rally. The key watch is the upcoming product roadmap and any supply‑chain constraints that could affect its growth momentum.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has slipped 5.2% on the day and remains 56.5% below its 52‑week high, though still 22.9% above its low, indicating a deep discount to recent peaks. The stock’s recent weakness follows broader tech pressure and a weak earnings outlook. Watch for any guidance updates or macro‑tech sentiment shifts as the next catalyst.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce is up modestly today but has surged 25.5% over the past week and sits just 2.6% shy of its 52‑week high, reflecting a strong rebound from a steep low. Momentum remains tied to its recent cloud‑software deals and AI integration. Investors should monitor the upcoming quarterly results for guidance on subscription growth.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan is marginally lower, trading 2.8% below its 52‑week high and 26.7% above its low, with modest YTD gains of 10.6%. The stock is holding steady amid stable earnings and interest‑rate expectations. Key focus will be the bank’s net interest margin trends and any Fed policy shifts.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America is near its 52‑week high, down 4.4% from that peak but 33.4% above its low, with a solid 12% YTD rise. The modest daily gain reflects a broadly stable banking sector. Watch the bank’s loan‑growth figures and credit‑quality metrics for next‑move signals.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa slipped 1.8% and is now 3.0% below its 52‑week high, still 26.6% above its low, with an 8.2% YTD gain. The dip follows broader payment‑card volatility. Investors should keep an eye on transaction volume trends and any shifts in consumer spending patterns.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard fell 1.4% and trades 3.1% under its 52‑week high, 23.4% above its low, posting a modest 3.7% YTD increase. The stock is sensitive to payment‑network usage and macro‑spending data. Next catalyst will be quarterly volume growth and any competitive pressure from new fintech entrants.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix is down 0.3% and remains 36.0% below its 52‑week high, though 19.5% above its low, with a 10.2% monthly gain offset by an 11.2% YTD decline. The recent bounce follows a price‑cut and content push. Watch subscriber churn and upcoming content slate performance for direction.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly rose 0.3% and sits 9.4% under its 52‑week high, still 63.4% above its low, with a 7.9% YTD rise. The stock is buoyed by strong pipeline expectations. Key watch is the rollout of its new diabetes and obesity drugs and any FDA decisions.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth gained 1.8% and trades 9.2% below its 52‑week high, 53.9% above its low, delivering a 19.4% YTD gain. The stock benefits from steady enrollment growth. Investors should focus on Medicare Advantage enrollment trends and cost‑inflation pressures.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson rallied 2.0% on the day and is up 6.3% month‑to‑date, sitting just 0.7% below its 52‑week high after a 32.9% YTD gain. The stock remains near the top of its range, so investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance and any news on its pharmaceutical pipeline for next‑move cues.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart edged up 1.0% today but is down 5.5% YTD, trading 20.9% off its 52‑week high and only 9.2% above its low. With margin pressure from higher wages, the key catalyst to monitor is the next same‑store sales report and any updates on its grocery‑to‑door strategy.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco slipped 0.4% on the day, down 14.0% from its 52‑week peak and 11.1% above its low, while posting a modest 10.5% YTD gain. Investors should focus on membership renewal trends and any shifts in discretionary spending that could affect its volume growth.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot fell 2.5% intraday, now 22.9% below its 52‑week high and 8.3% above its low, with a 6.2% YTD decline. The next driver will be the upcoming housing‑starts data and the company’s inventory positioning ahead of the spring build season.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil rose 2.2% today, trading just 2.8% shy of its 52‑week high after a 36.9% YTD surge. With oil prices volatile, the critical watch point is the next quarterly earnings and any updates on its capital‑allocation plan, especially dividend and buyback guidance.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola slipped 0.8% on the day, now 4.3% below its 52‑week high but still 36.7% above its low, delivering a 29.0% YTD rise. Investors should keep an eye on the upcoming earnings beat expectations and any progress on its premium‑product rollout and pricing strategy.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney dropped 1.2% intraday, sitting 9.3% under its 52‑week high and 15.8% above its low after a 10.4% monthly gain but a 4.3% YTD decline. The next key event is the performance of its streaming segment and the rollout of the new park attractions, which will drive short‑term sentiment.
